correctness.rationale: Homogeneity over the pointwise named base identifies complete types with finite adjacency patterns, and universality gives realization. The two independent old neighborhoods may overlap when the new pair is nonadjacent, and are disjoint exactly when the new pair is adjacent. For the sharpness check I classified triangle-free graphs directly by vertex and edge counts. The five-vertex classes have multiplicities 1,1,2,3,4,2,1 at edge counts 0 through 6. At four edges they are the three five-vertex trees and C4 plus an isolate; at five edges the cycle is C4 with a leaf or C5; at six edges an odd cycle is impossible (a chord of a spanning C5 creates a triangle), so the graph is K2,3. In a triangle-free graph i3=binom(n,3)−(n−2)e+sum_v binom(deg v,2); at n=5, i4 is the number of vertices incident to every edge. These formulas reproduce the sole collision at size five and distinguish all classes through size four. Exactly one member of the size-five collision is connected. Independent three-state summation gives 105, 103, 209, 203 in witness order, with first-subset-size breakdowns (14,47,36,8), (14,47,35,7), (19,81,87,22), (19,81,85,18); the other type components are the squares of 14 or 19, as claimed. In the six-vertex pentagon calculation, the factor printed as 20·1=40 is a transcription error: if the attachment vertex has nonzero state, the leaf has two allowed states, so the correct factor is 20·2=40. The exact Finding totals and conclusions are unaffected. The source checker was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The general type-count identities are covered, and later published entries recover the existence of the connected six-vertex example and its unequal two-type counts jointly by direct implication. The sharp combined classification has a distinct remainder: the first full independence-polynomial separation, the unique five-vertex collision, and the exclusion of connected witnesses below six under this full-polynomial comparison. The latter properties do not follow from the checked type-count or refined ordered-spectrum theorems.
residual_risks: A previously published short-order independence-equivalence table, including a relevant but inaccessible source, could settle the five-vertex classification without mentioning types. No claim of literature-wide priority is made.

value.rationale: This is a motivated reconstruction question for finite named bases: it locates precisely when the entire singleton-neighborhood histogram ceases to determine the next arity. The unique small obstruction and the higher minimum within connected bases give usable sharp test cases. The value is not the evaluation of a known type formula on a single graph, nor merely repeating a six-vertex example.
